- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Skrami promo video kit

Local workshop, never committed — ignored via `.git/info/exclude` (local-only, keeps `.gitignore` and
`git status` untouched). Move the `promo/` line into `.gitignore` if you'd rather have it declared there.

Made in Claude Code session **`379429ac-dc38-466c-b50d-f7acdc9b00fe`** (2026-09-29).
Resume it from the repo root: `claude --resume 379429ac-dc38-466c-b50d-f7acdc9b00fe`

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `skrami-promo-v2.mp4` | **current cut** — 62 s, 1920×1080, 60 fps, H.264 + AAC, synthesized lounge music at −32 LUFS, no chimes (copy on ~/Desktop/skrami-promo-v2.mp4) |
| `skrami-promo-v2.meta.json` | the take's length + chapter times — remix its music without re-recording (see Music) |
| `skrami-promo-v2-silent.mp4` | same cut, no audio |
| `stage.html` | the "set": per-topic backgrounds, dim + big-caption topic changes, keycap overlay, two fake browser windows holding the real app in iframes, fake cursors, title/end cards |
| `record.mjs` | Playwright script that performs the whole video against the real app; writes screencast frames + `frames/meta.json` (length, chapter times) |
| `music.py` | synthesizes the music from `meta.json`: tempo fitted to the video length |
| `render.sh` | one command: record → encode → music → mux → `render.mp4` + `render-silent.mp4` + `render.meta.json` (never overwrites the named takes); `render.sh v1` re-renders v1 |
| `stills/` | full-res frame per v2 scene (`0-title` … `8-end`, `transition-example`) — poster/thumbnail material |
| `skrami-promo-v2-web.mp4` | the published encode (crf 24 + AAC 128k from the master, 5.2 MB — visually equal, 40% smaller); this exact file is `src/client/promo.mp4` in the repo |
| `skrami-in-one-minute.mp4` | the GitHub README upload: starts on the finished title card, since GitHub has no poster support |
| `v1/` | the first approved cut (40 s, silent) with its own `stage.html`, `record.mjs`, stills |

## Re-render

```sh
pnpm dev              # repo root — the app on localhost:8787
promo/render.sh       # ~2 min → promo/render.mp4 + render-silent.mp4
```

Needs ffmpeg (brew), python3 (static server for the stage on 127.0.0.1:5190) and uv (numpy + scipy for the music,
fetched on the fly). `RECORD=0 node record.mjs` (with the stage server up) is a dry run that writes `shot-*.png`
checkpoints instead of frames. Music alone: `uv run --with numpy --with scipy music.py frames/meta.json music.wav`.

Nothing touches production: boards are minted on local wrangler dev (junk boards pile up in `.wrangler/` local state only).

## Storyboard (v2)

Every topic change = its own background color + the stage dims ~1 s with the caption big in the middle, then the
caption docks on top. (Audio chimes on topic changes were tried and removed at Roman's request — the visual cue is enough.) (Roman's v1 feedback: he watched the
examples and missed that the caption had moved on to the next feature.)

| t | Background | Caption | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–3 s | paper | — | title card: 4 sticky notes pop in, "Skrami", "An instant, no-signup, sticky-note scrum board." |
| 3–6 | yellow | One click. No signup. | index → Create board → board opens; address bar shows `/b/<name>-<id>` at navigation (v1 nit fixed) |
| 6–15 | blue | Stories are rows. Cards are sticky notes. | stories "Launch week", "Bug bash"; 3 cards via the popup |
| 15–21 | pink | Drag cards across the board. | real SortableJS drags → In Progress, → Done |
| 21–32 | green | Hover a card. Press a key. | Keybinds menu opens/closes; keycaps on screen: `I` move to In Progress, `D` move to Done, `C` new card right here → "Flaky test on CI" |
| 32–44 | lavender | Lock a board with a password. | ☰ → Set password… → `launch-week` → Save; Dana opens the link in a second window → unlock gate (zoomed for legibility) → types it → Open |
| 44–51 | peach | Share the link — everyone edits live. | Dana adds "Fix Safari drag glitch" → appears in Alex's window; Alex drags "Record demo video" → Verify → moves in Dana's |
| 51–58 | mint | AI agents can join too. `skrami.app/llms.txt` | raw WebSocket client per llms.txt: POST /auth for a token, joins as "Claude", creates + moves "Triage new bug reports", adds story "Beta feedback" with 2 cards |
| 58–62 | paper | — | end card: "Skrami", "No signup. Share the link.", `skrami.app` (held 3.8 s) |

Copy rules followed: captions reuse the product's own index-page wording, trimmed; no claims the product doesn't
make (e.g. no "free"); no Scrumy mention. Cast names (Alex, Dana, Claude) are placeholders.

## Music

All sounds are synthesized in `music.py` — no samples, nothing to license. Bossa-lounge in F major:
Fmaj9 – Dm9 – Gm9 – C13 – Am7 – D9 – Gm7 – C7, Rhodes-style FM electric piano comping, vibraphone melody (two
8-bar tunes, the third pass doubled an octave down on EP), upright-ish bass (root/fifth), shaker 16ths, 3-2 bossa
clave on rim, soft kick, pad, synthetic convolution reverb, gentle high shelf. Tempo is chosen so
2 intro + N×8 + 2 ending bars land exactly on the video length (v2: 109 bpm, 28 bars), so the final chord rings
under the end card. Mixed to −32 LUFS with a static gain (peaks ≈ −22 dBFS) — a quiet background bed. Checked by measurement only (band balance, chime lift,
loudness), not by ear — the AI that made it can't listen.

Roman's notes on the first v2 mix (−16 LUFS, chime gain 0.26, 5 dB duck): "make music quieter and dings a little bit
less pronounced (visual is great)" → −22 LUFS, chime gain 0.17 (≈ −3.5 dB), 3 dB duck. Then: "make audio twice as
quiet, and remove dings completely" → −32 LUFS (−10 dB = perceived half loudness) and chime + duck code deleted.
If it is ever wanted back: a two-note A5→C6 music-box bell (harmonic partials 1/2/3/4.2) at each chapter time, with
the music ducked under it — ~15 lines.

Remix the current take without re-recording:

```sh
uv run --with numpy --with scipy music.py skrami-promo-v2.meta.json music.wav
# then mux onto skrami-promo-v2-silent.mp4 with the two ffmpeg lines at the end of render.sh
```

## Storyboard (v2)

Every topic change = its own background color + the stage dims ~1 s with the caption big in the middle, then the
caption docks on top. (Audio chimes on topic changes were tried and removed at Roman's request — the visual cue is enough.) (Roman's v1 feedback: he watched the
examples and missed that the caption had moved on to the next feature.)

| t | Background | Caption | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–3 s | paper | — | title card: 4 sticky notes pop in, "Skrami", "An instant, no-signup, sticky-note scrum board." |
| 3–6 | yellow | One click. No signup. | index → Create board → board opens; address bar shows `/b/<name>-<id>` at navigation (v1 nit fixed) |
| 6–15 | blue | Stories are rows. Cards are sticky notes. | stories "Launch week", "Bug bash"; 3 cards via the popup |
| 15–21 | pink | Drag cards across the board. | real SortableJS drags → In Progress, → Done |
| 21–32 | green | Hover a card. Press a key. | Keybinds menu opens/closes; keycaps on screen: `I` move to In Progress, `D` move to Done, `C` new card right here → "Flaky test on CI" |
| 32–44 | lavender | Lock a board with a password. | ☰ → Set password… → `launch-week` → Save; Dana opens the link in a second window → unlock gate (zoomed for legibility) → types it → Open |
| 44–51 | peach | Share the link — everyone edits live. | Dana adds "Fix Safari drag glitch" → appears in Alex's window; Alex drags "Record demo video" → Verify → moves in Dana's |
| 51–58 | mint | AI agents can join too. `skrami.app/llms.txt` | raw WebSocket client per llms.txt: POST /auth for a token, joins as "Claude", creates + moves "Triage new bug reports", adds story "Beta feedback" with 2 cards |

## Music

All sounds are synthesized in `music.py` — no samples, nothing to license. Bossa-lounge in F major:
Fmaj9 – Dm9 – Gm9 – C13 – Am7 – D9 – Gm7 – C7, Rhodes-style FM electric piano comping, vibraphone melody (two
8-bar tunes, the third pass doubled an octave down on EP), upright-ish bass (root/fifth), shaker 16ths, 3-2 bossa
clave on rim, soft kick, pad, synthetic convolution reverb, gentle high shelf. Tempo is chosen so
2 intro + N×8 + 2 ending bars land exactly on the video length (v2: 109 bpm, 28 bars), so the final chord rings
under the end card. Mixed to −32 LUFS with a static gain (peaks ≈ −22 dBFS) — a quiet background bed. Checked by measurement only (band balance, chime lift,
loudness), not by ear — the AI that made it can't listen.

less pronounced (visual is great)" → −22 LUFS, chime gain 0.17 (≈ −3.5 dB), 3 dB duck. Then: "make audio twice as
quiet, and remove dings completely" → −32 LUFS (−10 dB = perceived half loudness) and chime + duck code deleted.

## How it works (and the rakes hit)

- **Resolution:** CDP `Page.startScreencast` returns CSS-pixel frames whatever `deviceScaleFactor` is (checked in both
  headless shell and new headless). So the viewport is 1920×1080 at DPR 1 and `stage.html` lays out at 1280×720 inside
  `#root` scaled 1.5× by a CSS transform — iframe content rasterizes crisp at the scaled size.
- **End-card hold:** a still end card emits no screencast frames, so the last frame must be held until the real stop
  time (`endTs = stopAt`). v1 predates this fix — its end card shows ~1.6 s instead of the scripted 3.6 s.
- **Cursors** live outside `#root` in viewport px (drawn 1.5×) so they stay sharp; `record.mjs` works in viewport px
  (`K = 1.5` for hand-placed coordinates). Eased moves with a slight arc; clicks show a ripple.
- **Z-order:** `#dim` (61) and `#caption` (62) sit above the title/end cards (60) so the first topic change covers
  the fading title instead of ghosting through it.
- **Two people = two origins.** Window 1 is `localhost:8787`, window 2 is `127.0.0.1:8787` — separate localStorage/IDB,
  so distinct clientId + `skrami:name` (Alex / Dana). Same wrangler dev, same Durable Object.
- **Password scene:** Dana's window loads the board only AFTER the password is set, so the gate is what she gets. The
  gate is enlarged with an injected `#gate main.gate { zoom: 1.7 }` (camera zoom on the real element; the board after
  unlock is untouched). The agent needs a token too: `POST /b/<id>/auth` → `hello` with `token`.
- **The stage must come from a local origin** (python http.server). A Playwright-routed fake host (`promo.test`) made
  both iframes fail to load — probably Chrome's local-network-access block (inference, not verified).
- **Selector trap:** `tbody tr` also matches the hidden Keybinds table in the board header → always `#board tbody tr`.
- **Drags:** real Playwright mouse (CDP input), paced by the glide loop, drives SortableJS fallback drags fine through
  the scaled cross-origin iframes. `locator.boundingBox()` returns viewport coordinates through the transforms.
- **Shortcuts:** `page.keyboard.press("KeyI")` etc. — the app matches on `e.code`; the pointer must be resting on the
  card (the app tracks hover via mouseover), and focus must be inside the iframe (any earlier click there does it).
- **Frames:** the screencast emits only on change (~60 fps during motion); an ffconcat list with per-frame durations
  → constant 60 fps via ffmpeg. The ffmpeg build here has no `drawtext` (no libfreetype) — no burned-in text via ffmpeg.

  split frame at 50.9 s, `preload="none"`). Commits `e014006` (SW: range requests bypass the cache — the Cache API
  rejects 206s), `782225d` (video + poster + build entries), `159a687` (byte ranges). Deployed manually.
- **Range rake:** Workers static assets answer `Range:` with the whole file (200, even on an edge HIT — verified with
  curl on prod). iOS Safari wants 206s, so `/promo.mp4` alone is `run_worker_first` and sliced by
  `src/server/range.ts` (tested in `test/range.test.ts`). WebKit on prod: `bytes=0-1 → 206`, seek to 0:45 plays.
  A re-cut under a new filename needs its path added to `run_worker_first` and the check in `worker.ts`.

  filename. `skrami-in-one-minute.mp4` = v2 trimmed by 1.45 s so frame 0 is the finished title card (0.3 s audio
  fade-in, crf 21, 6.3 MB < the 10 MB cap). Viewers start muted and must unmute for the music.
- **To update the site video:** re-encode the new master like the web file above, copy over `src/client/promo.mp4`
  (+ poster), commit, deploy. Each new cut adds ~5 MB to git history.

#!/bin/zsh
# Re-render the promo from the real app. Needs `pnpm dev` running in the repo root (localhost:8787).
#   ./render.sh      → current cut (v2): render.mp4 (with music) + render-silent.mp4
#   ./render.sh v1   → the v1 cut from v1/ (silent): v1/render.mp4
# Approved takes are never overwritten — rename a render to keep it.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
ROOT=$PWD
curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:8787/ || { echo "app not running — start it first: pnpm dev (repo root)"; exit 1; }
if lsof -tiTCP:5190 -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null; then echo "port 5190 busy — stop whatever serves it"; exit 1; fi
[ -d node_modules ] || npm install
npx playwright install chromium >/dev/null
[ "$1" = v1 ] && cd v1
[ -d frames ] && trash frames
python3 -m http.server 5190 --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
SRV=$!
trap "kill $SRV 2>/dev/null" EXIT
sleep 0.5
node record.mjs
V=render.mp4
[ "$1" = v1 ] || V=render-silent.mp4
ffmpeg -v error -y -f concat -safe 0 -i frames/list.ffconcat -fps_mode cfr -r 60 \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart $V
if [ "$1" != v1 ]; then
  cp frames/meta.json render.meta.json # chapter times — lets music.py remix a take without re-recording
  uv run --with numpy --with scipy "$ROOT/music.py" frames/meta.json frames/music.wav
  # static gain to -32 LUFS: a quiet background bed (Roman asked twice for quieter: -16 → -22 → -32)
  I=$(ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -i frames/music.wav -af ebur128=framelog=quiet -f null - 2>&1 | awk '$1=="I:"{v=$2} END{print v}')
  G=$(python3 -c "print(round(-32 - ($I), 2))")
  ffmpeg -v error -y -i $V -i frames/music.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy \
    -af "volume=${G}dB" -ar 48000 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -shortest -movflags +faststart render.mp4
fi
trash frames
echo "→ $PWD/render.mp4"

# Skryn

A lightweight macOS menu bar app for taking screenshots and annotating them.

## Installation

1. Download `Skryn.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/rsedykh/skryn/releases/latest)
2. Unzip and drag `Skryn.app` to your Applications folder
3. Right-click the app → Open on first launch (required for unsigned apps)
4. Grant Screen Recording permission when prompted

### Updating

Since the app is unsigned, macOS may revoke Screen Recording permission after updating. If screenshots stop working:

1. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording
2. Remove Skryn from the list
3. Re-add it; the app will prompt for permission again

## Usage

Click the camera icon in the menu bar or press **Cmd+Shift+5** (configurable in Settings) to capture your screen. An annotation window opens where you can draw before saving. You can also drag an image file onto the menu bar icon to open it for annotation.

**Shortcuts**

- **Drag** — Arrow
- **Shift + Drag** — Line
- **Cmd + Drag** — Rectangle
- **Option + Drag** — Crop
- **Control + Drag** — Blur
- **Esc** — Remove crop
- **Delete** — Remove hovered annotation
- **Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z** — Undo / Redo
- **T** — Type text at the cursor (over existing text, edits it)
- **U** — Insert capture time (UTC) at cursor
- **Cmd + + / Cmd + -** — Increase / Decrease text size
- **Shift + Enter** — new text line (Enter or Esc finishes the text; empty text is discarded)
- **Cmd+Enter** and **Option+Enter** and **Control+Enter** — Save to different locations (configurable in Settings)
- **Cmd+W** — Cancel screenshot

You can also hover over the annotation and change its size or drag it.

## Build

Requires Xcode and macOS.

```bash
xcodebuild -project Skryn/Skryn.xcodeproj -scheme Skryn -configuration Release build
```

# Skryn

A lightweight macOS menu bar app for taking screenshots and annotating them.

## Installation

1. Download `Skryn.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/rsedykh/skryn/releases/latest)
2. Unzip and drag `Skryn.app` to your Applications folder
3. Right-click the app → Open on first launch (required for unsigned apps)
4. Grant Screen Recording permission when prompted

### Updating

Since the app is unsigned, macOS may revoke Screen Recording permission after updating. If screenshots stop working:

1. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording
2. Remove Skryn from the list
3. Re-add it; the app will prompt for permission again

## Usage

Click the camera icon in the menu bar or press **Cmd+Shift+5** (configurable in Settings) to capture your screen. An annotation window opens where you can draw before saving. You can also drag an image file onto the menu bar icon to open it for annotation.

**Shortcuts**

- **Drag** — Arrow
- **Shift + Drag** — Line
- **Cmd + Drag** — Rectangle
- **Option + Drag** — Crop
- **Control + Drag** — Blur
- **Esc** — Remove crop
- **Delete** — Remove hovered annotation
- **Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z** — Undo / Redo
- **T** — Type text at the cursor (over existing text, edits it)
- **U** — Insert capture time (UTC) at cursor
- **Cmd + + / Cmd + -** — Increase / Decrease text size
- **Shift + Enter** — new text line (Enter or Esc finishes the text; empty text is discarded)
- **Cmd+Enter** and **Option+Enter** and **Control+Enter** — Save to different locations (configurable in Settings)
- **Cmd+W** — Cancel screenshot

You can also hover over the annotation and change its size or drag it.

## Build

Requires Xcode and macOS.

```bash
xcodebuild -project Skryn/Skryn.xcodeproj -scheme Skryn -configuration Release build
```

<!doctype html>
<html>
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<style>
  :root {
    --ink: #2b3440; --soft: #4b5563; --muted: #9ca3af;
    --paper: #f3efe7;
    --yellow: #fbefb0; --blue: #cfe2f6; --pink: #f7d6e2; --green: #d5eed3;
  }
  * { box-sizing: border-box; }
  html, body { margin: 0; width: 1920px; height: 1080px; overflow: hidden; }
  #root { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 1280px; height: 720px; transform: scale(1.5); transform-origin: 0 0; overflow: hidden; }
  body {
    font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif;
    color: var(--ink);
    background:
      radial-gradient(1350px 750px at 12% 0%, rgba(251, 239, 176, .55), transparent 70%),
      radial-gradient(1200px 780px at 100% 100%, rgba(207, 226, 246, .6), transparent 70%),
      radial-gradient(900px 600px at 95% 5%, rgba(247, 214, 226, .45), transparent 70%),
      var(--paper);
  }
  .serif { font-family: "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif; }
  /* ---------- captions ---------- */
  #caption {
    position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 30px; height: 56px;
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 18px;
    font-family: "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif; font-size: 34px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -.4px;
  }
  #caption { z-index: 62; } /* above the title/end cards too, so the first topic change covers the fading title */
  #caption .line { position: absolute; opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); transition: opacity .45s ease, transform .45s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); white-space: nowrap; }
  #caption .line.in { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
  #caption .line.out { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-8px); }
  /* a topic change: the caption lands big in the middle of a dimmed stage, then docks on top */
  #caption .line.big { transform: translateY(292px) scale(1.5); transition: opacity .35s ease, transform .7s cubic-bezier(.25,.8,.2,1); }
  #caption .line.big.in { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(292px) scale(1.5); }
  #caption .line.big.in.dock { transform: none; }
  /* ---------- per-topic backgrounds ---------- */
  .bg { position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0; transition: opacity 1s ease; }
  .bg.on { opacity: 1; }
  .bg { background: radial-gradient(1000px 620px at 4% 0%, var(--a), transparent 70%), radial-gradient(900px 640px at 100% 100%, var(--a), transparent 70%), radial-gradient(700px 420px at 70% 30%, var(--b), transparent 70%), var(--base); }

  .bg[data-t=yellow]   { --base: #f6eac0; --a: rgba(250, 214, 105, .55); --b: rgba(255, 248, 222, .75); }

import AppKit

// The director: performs the whole promo against Skryn's real AnnotationView, one 60 fps frame at a time.
//   promo-render <promo dir> <out.mp4>          full render + stills/ + <out>.meta.json
//   MODE=stills promo-render <promo dir> -      stills only (fast)
//   AT=4.2,9.5 promo-render <promo dir> -       just those moments → previews/

NSApplication.shared.setActivationPolicy(.prohibited)

let root = CommandLine.arguments[1]
let out = CommandLine.arguments[2]
let env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
let at: [Int] = (env["AT"] ?? "").split(separator: ",").compactMap { Double($0) }.map { Int(($0 * fps).rounded()) }
let stillsOnly = env["MODE"] == "stills"
let encoding = at.isEmpty && !stillsOnly

// ---------- assets ----------

let rectsJSON = try! JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(contentsOf: URL(fileURLWithPath: "\(root)/assets/rects.json")))
let rects: [String: CGRect] = (rectsJSON as! [String: [String: Double]]).mapValues {
    CGRect(x: $0["x"]!, y: $0["y"]!, width: $0["w"]!, height: $0["h"]!)
}
func R(_ id: String) -> CGRect { rects[id]! }

let stage = Stage(desks: [loadCG("\(root)/assets/desk-0.png"), loadCG("\(root)/assets/desk-1.png")],
                  icon: loadCG("\(root)/assets/icon.png"))
stage.shotRect = R("shot")

let ctx = makeContext(videoW, videoH)
let encoder = encoding ? Encoder(path: out) : nil
var frame = 0
var chapters: [[String: Any]] = []
var pendingStill: String?
try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: "\(root)/stills", withIntermediateDirectories: true)
try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: "\(root)/previews", withIntermediateDirectories: true)

func tick() {
    stage.t = Double(frame) / fps
    let want = encoding || at.contains(frame) || pendingStill != nil
    if want { stage.render(into: ctx) }
    encoder?.write(ctx)
    if let name = pendingStill {
        writePNG(ctx.makeImage()!, "\(root)/stills/\(name).png")
        pendingStill = nil
    }
    if at.contains(frame) { writePNG(ctx.makeImage()!, "\(root)/previews/\(String(format: "%05.2f", stage.t)).png") }
    frame += 1
    stage.t = Double(frame) / fps
}

func wait(_ d: Double) { for _ in 0..<Int((d * fps).rounded()) { tick() } }
func still(_ name: String) { pendingStill = name }

// ---------- the app ----------

var app: Skryn!

/// Screenshot point → screen point, once the annotation window is up.
func S(_ x: CGFloat, _ y: CGFloat) -> CGPoint { app.onScreen(CGPoint(x: x, y: y)) }

func hover() {
    guard stage.appVisible else { stage.cursorShape = .arrow; return }
    app.mouse(.mouseMoved, at: stage.cursor)
    stage.cursorShape = NSCursor.current
}

func bezier(_ a: CGPoint, _ c: CGPoint, _ b: CGPoint, _ t: Double) -> CGPoint {
    lerp(lerp(a, c, t), lerp(c, b, t), t)
}

/// Eased glide with a slight arc, hovering all the way like a real pointer.
func move(to p: CGPoint, _ d: Double, arc: CGFloat = 0.12) {
    let a = stage.cursor
    let mid = lerp(a, p, 0.5)
    let c = CGPoint(x: mid.x - (p.y - a.y) * arc, y: mid.y + (p.x - a.x) * arc)
    stage.cursorHidden = false
    let n = max(1, Int((d * fps).rounded()))
    for i in 1...n {
        stage.cursor = bezier(a, c, p, easeInOut(Double(i) / Double(n)))
        hover()
        tick()
    }
}

func drag(to p: CGPoint, _ d: Double, mods: NSEvent.ModifierFlags = []) {
    let a = stage.cursor
    app.mouse(.leftMouseDown, at: a, mods: mods)

}
func R(_ id: String) -> CGRect { rects[id]! }

                  icon: loadCG("\(root)/assets/icon.png"))

let ctx = makeContext(videoW, videoH)

var chapters: [[String: Any]] = []

try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: "\(root)/stills", withIntermediateDirectories: true)

func tick() {
    stage.t = Double(frame) / fps
    let want = encoding || at.contains(frame) || pendingStill != nil
    if want { stage.render(into: ctx) }
    encoder?.write(ctx)
    if let name = pendingStill {
        writePNG(ctx.makeImage()!, "\(root)/stills/\(name).png")
        pendingStill = nil
    }
    if at.contains(frame) { writePNG(ctx.makeImage()!, "\(root)/previews/\(String(format: "%05.2f", stage.t)).png") }
    frame += 1
    stage.t = Double(frame) / fps
}

func wait(_ d: Double) { for _ in 0..<Int((d * fps).rounded()) { tick() } }
func still(_ name: String) { pendingStill = name }

var app: Skryn!

/// Screenshot point → screen point, once the annotation window is up.
func S(_ x: CGFloat, _ y: CGFloat) -> CGPoint { app.onScreen(CGPoint(x: x, y: y)) }

func hover() {
    guard stage.appVisible else { stage.cursorShape = .arrow; return }
    app.mouse(.mouseMoved, at: stage.cursor)
    stage.cursorShape = NSCursor.current
}

func bezier(_ a: CGPoint, _ c: CGPoint, _ b: CGPoint, _ t: Double) -> CGPoint {
    lerp(lerp(a, c, t), lerp(c, b, t), t)
}

/// Eased glide with a slight arc, hovering all the way like a real pointer.
func move(to p: CGPoint, _ d: Double, arc: CGFloat = 0.12) {
    let a = stage.cursor
    let mid = lerp(a, p, 0.5)
    let c = CGPoint(x: mid.x - (p.y - a.y) * arc, y: mid.y + (p.x - a.x) * arc)
    stage.cursorHidden = false
    let n = max(1, Int((d * fps).rounded()))
    for i in 1...n {
        stage.cursor = bezier(a, c, p, easeInOut(Double(i) / Double(n)))
        hover()
        tick()
    }
}

func drag(to p: CGPoint, _ d: Double, mods: NSEvent.ModifierFlags = []) {
    let a = stage.cursor
    app.mouse(.leftMouseDown, at: a, mods: mods)
    stage.cursorDown = true
    tick()
    let n = max(1, Int((d * fps).rounded()))
    for i in 1...n {
        stage.cursor = lerp(a, p, easeInOut(Double(i) / Double(n)))
        app.mouse(.leftMouseDragged, at: stage.cursor, mods: mods)
        stage.cursorShape = NSCursor.current
        tick()
    }
    app.mouse(.leftMouseUp, at: p, mods: mods)
    stage.cursorDown = false
    hover()
    tick()
}

func topic(_ name: String, _ text: String, _ bg: Backdrop) {
    chapters.append(["name": name, "t": stage.t])
    stage.topic(text, bg)
}

/// A modifier + drag tool: keycaps up, glide to the start, hold the keys, drag.
func tool(_ keys: [String], _ label: String, from a: CGPoint, to b: CGPoint, mods: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) {
    stage.showHUD(keys.map { .key($0) } + [.key("Drag"), .label(label)])
    move(to: a, 0.42)
    stage.pressed = Set(0...keys.count)
    wait(0.08)
    drag(to: b, 0.46, mods: mods)
    stage.pressed = []
    wait(0.34)
}

/// Keycap hit: pressed look for a moment around the real key event.
func hit(_ indices: Set<Int>, _ action: () -> Void, hold: Double = 0.14) {
    stage.pressed.formUnion(indices)
    action()
    wait(hold)
    stage.pressed.subtract(indices)
}

#!/bin/zsh
# Renders the promo from the real app code, start to finish:
#   shoot the staged desktop → build the renderer against ../Skryn/Skryn → 60 fps frames → music → mux
#   ./render.sh          → render.mp4 (with music) + render-silent.mp4 + render.meta.json + stills/
#   MODE=stills ./render.sh   → stills/ only (seconds)
# Approved takes are never overwritten — rename a render to keep it.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
[ -d node_modules ] || npm install
node shoot.mjs
[ -f assets/icon-cut.png ] || uv run --quiet --with pillow icon.py ../docs/icon.png assets/icon-cut.png
./build.sh
if [ "$MODE" = stills ]; then build/promo-render $PWD -; exit; fi
build/promo-render $PWD render-silent.mp4
uv run --quiet --with numpy --with scipy music.py render-silent.meta.json build/music.wav
mv render-silent.meta.json render.meta.json
# static gain to -32 LUFS: the quiet background bed Roman settled on for the Skrami promo
I=$(ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -i build/music.wav -af ebur128=framelog=quiet -f null - 2>&1 | awk '$1=="I:"{v=$2} END{print v}')
G=$(python3 -c "print(round(-32 - ($I), 2))")
ffmpeg -v error -y -i render-silent.mp4 -i build/music.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy \
  -af "volume=${G}dB" -ar 48000 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -shortest -movflags +faststart render.mp4
echo "→ $PWD/render.mp4"
EOF
chmod +x render.sh && time ./render.sh 2>&1 | tail -5

# Skryn promo video kit

A local workshop that is never committed. It's ignored via `.git/info/exclude`, the same setup as the Skrami promo kit.

Made in Claude Code session **`3b941364-f907-413c-9f23-521f75ebcbac`** (2026-09-29).
Resume it from the repo root: `claude --resume 3b941364-f907-413c-9f23-521f75ebcbac`

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `skryn-promo-v1.mp4` | **current cut**: 41.5 s, 1920×1080, 60 fps, H.264 + AAC, synthesized lounge bed at −32 LUFS |
| `skryn-promo-v1-web.mp4` | web encode (crf 24, AAC 128k), 4.5 MB |
| `skryn-promo-v1-silent.mp4` | same cut, no audio |
| `skryn-promo-v1.meta.json` | length + chapter times, so `music.py` can remix without re-rendering |
| `poster.jpg` | poster frame: the finished annotation with the crop being drawn, at ~31 s |
| `stills/` | one full-res frame per scene (`0-title` … `7-end`) + `exported.png`, the exact image ⌘⏎ put on the clipboard |
| `stage/desktop.html` | the staged Mac desktop Skryn captures: a browser on `console.example.com` (fictional, reserved domain) + a chat with "Dana" |
| `shoot.mjs` | Playwright: shoots the desktop at 2× (`assets/desk-0.png`, `desk-1.png` after the paste) + `assets/rects.json` (targets, in screen points) |
| `render/` | the renderer, in Swift: `main.swift` = the storyboard as code, `App.swift` = drives the real `AnnotationView`, `Stage.swift` = camera/desktop/cursor/captions/keycaps/cards, `Encoder.swift` = ffmpeg pipe, `Kit.swift` = tweens + drawing helpers |
| `build.sh` | compiles `render/` together with `../Skryn/Skryn/*.swift` (minus `SkrynApp.swift`) into one binary |
| `render.sh` | one command: shoot → build → frames → music → mux. Writes `render.mp4`, `render-silent.mp4` and `render.meta.json`, and never overwrites the named takes |
| `music.py` | copied from the Skrami kit: bossa lounge, every sound synthesized, tempo fitted to the video length |
| `icon.py` | knocks the white square out of `docs/icon.png` so the icon sits cleanly on the title and end cards |

## Re-render

```sh
promo/render.sh                  # ~2 min → promo/render.mp4 + render-silent.mp4 + render.meta.json + stills/
MODE=stills promo/render.sh      # ~5 s → stills/ only, for checking a change
AT=4.2,18.4 promo/build/promo-render $PWD/promo -   # just those moments → promo/previews/
```

Needs Xcode's `swiftc`, Homebrew ffmpeg, node (Playwright 1.63, which uses the cached Chromium) and uv (numpy + scipy for the music, pillow for the icon).
It needs no Screen Recording or Accessibility permission and never takes over the screen. Everything renders offscreen, frame by frame.

## What's real and what's staged

- **Real:** everything inside the annotation window. It's Skryn's own `AnnotationView` from `../Skryn/Skryn`, compiled in and fed synthetic `NSEvent`s: modifier drags pick the tool, hovering shows handles, a handle drag retargets the arrow, and `C`, `⌫`, digits, `T`, `⌘=` and `⏎` all go through the real key paths. ⌘Z calls the menu action `undo(_:)`, and ⌘⏎ runs the real `SaveAction` path, which closes the window. The pointer shapes come from `NSCursor.current` after each event (crosshair on handles, open hand on bodies). The window is sized with `AnnotationWindow`'s own math (84% of the screen). The image pasted into the chat is `compositeAsCGImage()`, byte for byte what the clipboard would get.
- **Staged:** the desktop, the menu bar (Skryn's real `camera` SF Symbol), the cursor position, the window shadow, the camera zooms, the captions, the keycaps and the chat reaction. The ~0.1 s between the "5" keycap and the window is a stand-in for ScreenCaptureKit's capture time. The app shows its window with no animation, and so does the video. The text caret is drawn by the stage at the text view's real insertion rect, because NSTextView blinks it on a timer the renderer never runs. The pointer hides while typing, as macOS does.
- **One patch to the app code, in the build copy only:** `build.sh` makes `compositeAsCGImage()` non-private in `build/app/AnnotationView.swift` and fails loudly if that line ever changes.

## Storyboard (v1)

Every topic change gets its own background color. The stage dims about 1 s with the caption big in the middle, then the caption docks on top. This is the same device as the Skrami v2 promo.

| t | Background | Caption | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–1.9 s | paper | — | title card: icon, "Skryn", "Screenshot & Annotate menu bar app" (the site's tagline) |
| 1.9–6.1 | blue | One hotkey. Instant capture. | desktop as a display; keycaps `⇧ ⌘ 5` → annotation window pops over it; camera to the window, desktop fades |
| 6.1–14.3 | peach | Hold a key. Pick a tool. | push in on the page: `Drag` arrow (aimed roughly), `⌘` rectangle around the test key, `⇧⌘` ellipse on the API keys tab, `⇧` line under the warning, `⌃` blur over the production key |
| 14.3–22.0 | green | Press a digit. Press T. | badges `1` Settings, `2` API keys tab, `3` Test row; `T` → types "Copy the test key", `⌘+` twice, `⏎` |
| 22.0–28.1 | lavender | Everything stays editable. | drag the arrow's handle onto Copy; `C` turns the rectangle blue; `⌫` deletes the underline; `⌘Z` brings it back |
| 28.1–37.7 | yellow | Crop, then ⌘⏎ to copy. | pull back; `⌥` crop to the page; `⌘⏎` → window gone; camera to the chat; `⌘V` → the exported image lands, push in; Dana: "Perfect, thanks!"; keycaps `⌥⏎ save to folder`, `⌃⏎ upload, copy link` |
| 37.7–41.5 | paper | — | end card: icon, "Skryn", "Native macOS. No account required." (site wording), `skryn.app` |

Copy rules: captions only claim what the app does, and the end card reuses the site's own words. There's no "free" and no speed numbers. The product is fictional (Example Cloud on `console.example.com`, a reserved domain), and Alex and Dana are placeholder names.

## How it works (and the rakes hit)

- **Undo grouping:** NSUndoManager puts everything registered in one run-loop pass into one undo step. Driven without a run loop, ⌘Z undid the whole session. Calling `endUndoGrouping()` by hand breaks its auto-grouping state and throws on the next registration. The fix is to let `RunLoop.main` turn once after every event (`Skryn.endOfEventLoop`). It fatal-errors if a group is ever left open.
- **Badges combine on wall time:** digits within 0.5 s of real time merge (1, 2 → 12). The renderer runs faster than real time, so `Skryn.key` sleeps until 0.6 s of wall time separate digit presses.
- **Pointer position:** badges and `T` read `window.mouseLocationOutsideOfEventStream`, so `StageWindow` overrides it to report the scripted cursor.
- **Crispness:** the view renders at 3× via `cacheDisplay(in:to:)` into a 3× bitmap rep, and the desktop is shot at 2×. The deepest push-in (2.1×) stays at or below 1:1.
- **Tweens are segment lists:** a second `go()` used to overwrite the first, so "dim in now, out later" skipped the fade-in.
- **Content mask:** content fades out under the caption band with a `.destinationIn` gradient. It needs `.drawsBeforeStartLocation`, or everything above the gradient stays opaque.
- **Stills** render the current state immediately. Deferring to the next frame caught the first frame of the next topic.
- `Encoder` is a Swift stdlib protocol, so the class is `FrameEncoder`. Compiled into the app's module, the name would shadow it.

## Ideas for next iterations (not done)

- Show `⌃⏎` for real: menu bar icon cycling the 8 arrow symbols (120 ms, like `AppDelegate`), then the link pasted into the chat.
- Drag-and-drop an image onto the menu bar icon; `U` capture-time stamp; `Esc` to remove a crop; Settings (per-action modifier, hotkey recorder).
- Shorter ~25 s cut: tools + ⌘⏎ + paste only. A 1:1 or 9:16 social cut.
- Dark-mode desktop.
- Different music (key/tempo), or none.

| 6.1–14.3 | peach | Hold a key. Pick a tool. | push in on the page: `Drag` arrow (aimed roughly), `⌘` rectangle around the test key, `⇧⌘` ellipse on the API keys tab, `⇧` line under the warning, `⌃` blur over the production key |
| 14.3–22.0 | green | Press a digit. Press T. | badges `1` Settings, `2` API keys tab, `3` Test row; `T` → types "Copy the test key", `⌘+` twice, `⏎` |
| 22.0–28.1 | lavender | Everything stays editable. | drag the arrow's handle onto Copy; `C` turns the rectangle blue; `⌫` deletes the underline; `⌘Z` brings it back |
| 28.1–37.7 | yellow | Crop, then ⌘⏎ to copy. | pull back; `⌥` crop to the page; `⌘⏎` → window gone; camera to the chat; `⌘V` → the exported image lands, push in; Dana: "Perfect, thanks!"; keycaps `⌥⏎ save to folder`, `⌃⏎ upload, copy link` |
| 37.7–41.5 | paper | — | end card: icon, "Skryn", "Native macOS. No account required." (site wording), `skryn.app` |

Copy rules: captions only claim what the app does, and the end card reuses the site's own words. There's no "free" and no speed numbers. The product is fictional (Example Cloud on `console.example.com`, a reserved domain), and Alex and Dana are placeholder names.

## How it works (and the rakes hit)

- **Undo grouping:** NSUndoManager puts everything registered in one run-loop pass into one undo step. Driven without a run loop, ⌘Z undid the whole session. Calling `endUndoGrouping()` by hand breaks its auto-grouping state and throws on the next registration. The fix is to let `RunLoop.main` turn once after every event (`Skryn.endOfEventLoop`). It fatal-errors if a group is ever left open.
- **Badges combine on wall time:** digits within 0.5 s of real time merge (1, 2 → 12). The renderer runs faster than real time, so `Skryn.key` sleeps until 0.6 s of wall time separate digit presses.
- **Pointer position:** badges and `T` read `window.mouseLocationOutsideOfEventStream`, so `StageWindow` overrides it to report the scripted cursor.
- **Crispness:** the view renders at 3× via `cacheDisplay(in:to:)` into a 3× bitmap rep, and the desktop is shot at 2×. The deepest push-in (2.1×) stays at or below 1:1.
- **Tweens are segment lists:** a second `go()` used to overwrite the first, so "dim in now, out later" skipped the fade-in.
- **Content mask:** content fades out under the caption band with a `.destinationIn` gradient. It needs `.drawsBeforeStartLocation`, or everything above the gradient stays opaque.
- **Stills** render the current state immediately. Deferring to the next frame caught the first frame of the next topic.
- `Encoder` is a Swift stdlib protocol, so the class is `FrameEncoder`. Compiled into the app's module, the name would shadow it.

## Ideas for next iterations (not done)

- Show `⌃⏎` for real: menu bar icon cycling the 8 arrow symbols (120 ms, like `AppDelegate`), then the link pasted into the chat.
- Drag-and-drop an image onto the menu bar icon; `U` capture-time stamp; `Esc` to remove a crop; Settings (per-action modifier, hotkey recorder).
- Shorter ~25 s cut: tools + ⌘⏎ + paste only. A 1:1 or 9:16 social cut.
- Dark-mode desktop.
- Different music (key/tempo), or none.

Yes, and v1 is rendered: **`promo/skryn-promo-v1.mp4`**, 41.5 s at 1080p60 with music. There's also a 4.5 MB web encode (`skryn-promo-v1-web.mp4`) and a `poster.jpg`. To watch: `! open promo/skryn-promo-v1.mp4`

**How it works for a desktop app:** everything inside the Skryn window is your actual `AnnotationView`. The renderer compiles it straight from `Skryn/Skryn/*.swift`, sends it scripted mouse and key events, and draws it offscreen one frame at a time. The tools, hover handles, cursor shapes, text editor, blur and crop overlay are your app's own drawing. The image pasted into the chat at the end is exactly what ⌘⏎ puts on the clipboard. It needs no Screen Recording or Accessibility permission and never takes over your screen.

**What's staged:**
- **The desktop:** a browser on a fictional `console.example.com` page plus a chat window.
- **The rest of the frame:** the menu bar, cursor path, camera zooms, keycap pop-ups and captions.

**Storyboard.** It uses the same per-topic background color + dimmed big caption device as the Skrami v2 promo:
1. Title card.
2. "One hotkey. Instant capture.": `⇧⌘5` pops the window over the desktop.
3. "Hold a key. Pick a tool.": arrow, rectangle, ellipse, line and blur, each shown with its modifier keycap.
4. "Press a digit. Press T.": badges 1–3, then typing "Copy the test key" and `⌘+` twice.
5. "Everything stays editable.": dragging a handle, `C` to recolor, `⌫`, then `⌘Z`.
6. "Crop, then ⌘⏎ to copy.": `⌥` crop, `⌘⏎`, then `⌘V` into the chat, a "Perfect, thanks!" reply, and keycaps for the other two save modes.
7. End card with `skryn.app`.

The captions only use wording from your site or plain descriptions of what the app does.

**Things to know:**
- **Music:** I reused Skrami's synthesized track at the same quiet −32 LUFS level. I can't listen to audio, so I only checked it by measurement.
- **Timing:** everything happens at the frame the input arrives, which matches how instantly the app responds. The only invented delay is 0.1 s standing in for the screen capture.
- **Bugs fixed along the way:** with no event loop running, ⌘Z undid the whole session at once, and badges merged into one number. Both are fixed in the renderer; no app code changed. The kit's `README.md` covers these and other details.

The kit lives in `promo/` and stays out of git (`.git/info/exclude`, like Skrami's), so `git status` is clean. `promo/render.sh` re-renders everything in about 2 minutes.

I haven't added it to the website. Once you're happy with the cut, I can embed the web encode and poster in `docs/index.html`.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Skryn — Screenshot and Annotate for macOS</title>
  <meta name="description" content="A lightweight macOS menu bar app for taking screenshots and annotating them. Arrows, lines, rectangles, ellipses, blur, text, badges, crop — then copy, save, or upload.">
  <link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="icon.png">
  <style>
    * { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }

    :root {
      --bg: #fafafa;
      --text: #1a1a1a;
      --muted: #666;
      --border: #e0e0e0;
      --card-bg: #fff;
      --kbd-bg: #f0f0f0;
      --kbd-border: #d0d0d0;
      --accent: #1a1a1a;
      --link: #4a90d9;
    }

    @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      :root {
        --bg: #111;
        --text: #e8e8e8;
        --muted: #999;
        --border: #2a2a2a;
        --card-bg: #1a1a1a;
        --kbd-bg: #252525;
        --kbd-border: #333;
        --accent: #fff;
        --link: #6ab0f3;
      }
    }

    body {
      font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif;
      background: var(--bg);
      color: var(--text);
      line-height: 1.6;
      -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
    }

    a { color: var(--link); }

    .container {
      max-width: 640px;
      margin: 0 auto;
      padding: 0 24px;
    }

    /* Hero */
    .hero {
      text-align: center;
      padding: 80px 0 48px;
    }

    .hero img {
      width: 128px;
      height: 128px;
      border-radius: 28px;
      margin-bottom: 24px;
    }

    .hero h1 {
      font-size: 36px;
      font-weight: 700;
      letter-spacing: -0.5px;
      margin-bottom: 8px;
    }

    .hero .tagline {
      font-size: 18px;
      color: var(--muted);
      margin-bottom: 32px;
    }

    .download-btn {
      display: inline-block;
      background: var(--accent);
      color: var(--bg);
      text-decoration: none;
      padding: 12px 32px;
      border-radius: 8px;
      font-size: 16px;
      font-weight: 600;
      transition: opacity 0.15s;
    }

    .download-btn:hover { opacity: 0.8; }

    .download-note {
      font-size: 13px;
      color: var(--muted);
      margin-top: 12px;
    }

    /* Features */
    .features {
      padding: 48px 0;
    }

    .features h2 {
      font-size: 14px;
      font-weight: 600;
      text-transform: uppercase;
      letter-spacing: 1px;
      color: var(--muted);
      margin-bottom: 24px;
    }

    .feature-grid {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
      gap: 16px;
    }

    .feature {
      background: var(--card-bg);
      border: 1px solid var(--border);
      border-radius: 12px;
      padding: 20px;
    }

    .feature .title {
      font-weight: 600;
      font-size: 15px;
      margin-bottom: 4px;
    }

    .feature .desc {
      font-size: 14px;
      color: var(--muted);
    }

    /* Shortcuts */
    .shortcuts {
      padding: 48px 0;
    }

    .shortcuts h2 {
      font-size: 14px;
      font-weight: 600;
      text-transform: uppercase;
      letter-spacing: 1px;
      color: var(--muted);
      margin-bottom: 24px;
    }

    .shortcut-list {
      list-style: none;
      columns: 2;
      column-gap: 24px;
    }

    .shortcut-list li {
      display: flex;
      justify-content: space-between;
      align-items: center;
      padding: 10px 0;
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
      font-size: 14px;
    }

    .shortcut-list .keys {
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 6px;
      flex-shrink: 0;
    }

    kbd {
      background: var(--kbd-bg);
      border: 1px solid var(--kbd-border);
      border-radius: 5px;
      padding: 2px 8px;
      font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", sans-serif;
      font-size: 13px;
      white-space: nowrap;
    }

    /* Install */
    .install {
      padding: 48px 0;
    }

    .install h2 {
      font-size: 14px;
      font-weight: 600;
      text-transform: uppercase;
      letter-spacing: 1px;
      color: var(--muted);
      margin-bottom: 24px;
    }

    .install ol {
      padding-left: 20px;
    }

    .install li {
      font-size: 15px;
      margin-bottom: 8px;
    }

    /* Footer */
    footer {
      text-align: center;
      padding: 48px 0;
      font-size: 13px;
      color: var(--muted);
      border-top: 1px solid var(--border);
    }

content.text:
The video is live on https://skryn.app, directly under the Download button. I pushed it to `main` as `bb443a4`, the Pages build finished, and I played it on the live site in WebKit (the engine behind Safari) with no errors.

- **Source:** the page plays the upload you linked. It's byte-identical to `skryn-promo-v1-web.mp4`, so no video went into the repo. The only new file is the 124 KB poster frame, `docs/promo-poster.jpg`.
- **Layout:** 960px wide on desktop, wider than the 640px text column, so the keycaps and annotations stay readable. On phones it's full width.
- **Playback:** click to play, with the poster frame, no autoplay and nothing preloaded until then.

One risk: GitHub doesn't officially support linking to `user-attachments` from outside GitHub. It works today, but if GitHub ever blocks it, the fix is to commit the 4.5 MB mp4 into `docs/` and point the page at that.

I didn't run lint or tests, because only the HTML page and the poster changed. The push also triggered a hook of yours that printed "[entire] Pushing session logs to origin...".
